plan.topic: Surgery outcomes on GLP-1 medicines: 2.03 million elective-surgery records linked GLP-1 use to lower odds of major heart complications and infections (ANESTHESIOLOGY, Oct 2026, observational)
plan.angle: Title: 'GLP-1 Medicines (Like Mounjaro) and Surgery: Fewer Heart Complications?' First line: 'In about 2 million surgery records, people taking GLP-1 medicines had 11% lower odds of major heart complications after elective surgery. That's a link, not proof.' Give the population (adults, elective surgery over 1 hour, at least 24 hours in hospital, 2016–2024, 145,610 on a GLP-1) and the 8% lower odds of infection. Credit 'presented at the ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 meeting', plus the researchers' line that it doesn't prove cause and effect. Practical line: 'Tell your surgeon and anesthesia team you take a GLP-1, because these medicines can slow stomach emptying, and follow their plan.' One GI line and the prescriber line. On screen: 'observational · conference data · elective surgery >1 hr · odds, not proof'.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) or Semaglutide Before Surgery: Fewer Heart Complications?
plan.why: Published Oct 18 with low competition, so we're early. It builds on our anesthesia Short (83 views), puts a named drug first in a question title, and is a positive benefits-beyond-weight angle. | fact-check: The study exists, but its venue is misdescribed. It was presented at the ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 annual meeting (the ASA conference) in Oct 2026, not published in the journal Anesthesiology, so it's a conference abstract that hasn't been peer-reviewed in full (Newswise / ASA press release, MedicalXpress Oct 2026). Confirmed: 2,028,601 adults had elective surgery lasting more than 1 hour with at least 24 hours in hospital, Jan 2016–Dec 2024, and 145,610 were on GLP-1 therapy. Results: 11% lower odds of major cardiovascular complications (heart attack, heart injury, stroke or death) and 8% lower odds of postoperative infection. The authors say it doesn't prove cause and effect. Fixes: (a) on-screen and spoken attribution becomes 'presented at the ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 meeting, not yet a full published paper'; (b) the press materials may not give absolute rates per group. If the abstract doesn't, don't invent them: say 'absolute rates weren't reported in the summary'; (c) the working title implies tirzepatide and semaglutide were tested specifically, but the study covers GLP-1 therapy in general. Lead with 'GLP-1 medicines' and use brands only as recognisable examples, if the source names them; (d) in 2016–2024 most users were probably on older GLP-1s, so don't claim drug-specific results; (e) don't confirm the 'matched' claim unless the source says it. Keep 'tell your surgeon and anesthesia team', with no holding or timing advice.

package.title: On a GLP-1 before surgery? What 2M records show #shorts
package.description:
Quick answer: In 2.03 million records of elective surgery over an hour with at least 24 hours in hospital (2016–2024), GLP-1 users had 11% lower odds of major heart complications (about 1% vs 1.1% without) and 8% lower odds of infections (4.9% vs 5.3%). A link, not proof; ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 conference data, not yet published. Tell your surgical team and don't stop on your own. Common side effects: nausea, diarrhea, constipation.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

New data, not proof of cause: in 2.03 million records of elective surgery over an hour with at least 24 hours in hospital (2016–2024), adults taking a GLP-1 medicine had lower odds of major heart complications and infections after surgery.

What the records showed (matched 114,249 GLP-1 users vs 360,168 similar non-users):
Major heart complications — heart attack, heart injury, stroke or death from any cause: about 1% on a GLP-1 vs 1.1% without, 11% lower odds.
Infections after surgery: 4.9% vs 5.3%, 8% lower odds.
This is conference data from the ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 meeting, not yet a full published paper, and it looked at GLP-1 medicines as a group.
GLP-1s can slow stomach emptying — tell your surgeon and anesthesia team you're taking one, and follow their plan rather than stopping on your own.
Common side effects: nausea, diarrhea, constipation.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number in the Short against the sources and they all hold up. The study was presented at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 in San Diego (ASA release dated 18 Oct 2026) by Josephine Tolan, MD, of UTHealth Houston. It used Epic Cosmos data on 2,028,601 adults in the US who had elective surgery lasting over 60 minutes and stayed in hospital at least 24 hours, from 2016 to 2024. Of these, 145,610 were taking a GLP-1. After matching, 114,249 GLP-1 users were compared with 360,168 non-users (Inside Precision Medicine). Major heart complications were 1% vs 1.1% (OR 0.89, which is the "11% lower odds"). Infections were 4.9% vs 5.3% (OR 0.92, the "8% lower odds"). These rates come from Newsweek and Inside Precision Medicine. The script frames it correctly: observational, linked not causal, conference data not yet published, absolute rates shown next to the odds, and a "don't stop it on your own" safety line. The tell-your-surgical-team advice matches the delayed stomach emptying and aspiration warnings in the GLP-1 drug labels. Both label PDFs open, but their text couldn't be read through the tool. The hook pays off within 8 seconds and is hedged in the next line. Four small fixes, listed below: one wording addition ("from any cause"), one source tag, one caveat wording, and one unconfirmed label date.

issues.claim: Major heart complications meant heart attack, heart injury, stroke or death from any cause
issues.problem: The sources define the outcome only as 'heart attack, heart injury (myocardial injury), stroke and death'. None of them says 'from any cause', so this adds scope the sources don't give.
issues.fix: Major heart complications meant heart attack, heart injury, stroke or death: about 1% on a GLP-1 vs 1.1% without. Infections after surgery: 4.9% vs 5.3%, or 8% lower odds.

issues.location: s5 visual list item 5 and source_ids
issues.problem: This caveat appears only in Inside Precision Medicine (src5): the study 'did not assess whether continuing or withholding GLP-1s immediately before surgery influenced outcomes'. It is tagged to src1 and src4, which don't say it. 'Didn't track' is also stronger than 'didn't assess whether it influenced outcomes'. And the caveat appears on screen only, not in the narration.
issues.fix: Change the list item to "Didn't test pausing before surgery". Set source_ids to ["src1","src4","src5"]. Optionally end the narration with: "...it looked at GLP-1s as a group, and it didn't test pausing them before surgery."

issues.claim: people taking GLP-1 medicines had 11% lower odds of major heart complications after elective surgery
issues.problem: The 11% comes from the matched, adjusted analysis. 'Had' sounds slightly firmer than the source's 'was associated with'. The s2 hedge follows straight away, so this is acceptable, but 'were linked to' fits the evidence better.
issues.fix: Surgery coming up on a GLP-1? In about 2 million surgery records, GLP-1 medicines were linked to 11% lower odds of major heart complications after elective surgery.

issues.claim: Zepbound PI year 2026; Wegovy PI year 2025
issues.problem: Both PDFs open at the listed URLs, but I couldn't read their text to confirm the latest revision dates.
issues.fix: Before publishing, check the 'Revised: MM/YYYY' line on each PDF and set the year field to match.
